svg.text: CHAPTERS 6A TO 6C · THE BUYERS, THE BIDDERS, THE VENDORS
Three parties at the door
Three short chapters ask the same questions of one party each: who they are, what they need from the tender,
and what a published check gives them. Every line below is a sentence of its chapter, shortened.
The buyers
more bids than eyes
Their question: what should the work cost?
WHAT THEY NEED
Volume handled without hiring
Decisions that survive a challenge
The door kept open, as the law asks
Time back: funds freed sooner
Capacity on jobs too big for one head
WHAT A PUBLISHED CHECK GIVES THEM
Same bid, same answer, measured miss
No cap, no key, no fee at the door
Claims checked against evidence
A shorter tender, an earlier award
THE CATCH
Two answers to one bid invite a claim;
their records become the market's memory.
The bidders
racing for the light
Their question: what will it cost us, and
what will it take to win?
WHAT THEY NEED
A check before the bid goes in
Trust in bids a manager did not build
Fewer wasted bids: five in six lose
Same bid, same answer, reasons given
Room to spread the price their own way
Their own data kept their own
WHAT A PUBLISHED CHECK GIVES THEM
A cheaper bid, with the margin covered
A growing pie: more projects built
The surgical team in as a principal
Proof of life in a polished thicket
THE CATCH
The record proves what they knew;
everyone leaning on the same bot.
not for sale
The vendors
players, not referees
Their terms: the user verifies, and the
user pays.
WHAT THEY NEED
A strict, public format to build to
Demand from users carrying the risk
Protection from the general models
Their moat kept: data, service, habit
WHAT A PUBLISHED CHECK GIVES THEM
Test-takers, not targets
The referee nobody is building
A premium an underwriter can price
The sun was never for sale
THE CATCH
Credible cheap code squeezes margins;
every incumbent wants the pen.
The chapters say the rest: who each party is, sorted by what its door looks like when the thicket arrives.
